scope: Standalone staged IPv4 NAT component; not attached or activated by the node agent.

kernel.environment: Disposable Fedora 44 VM on SSH port 22291; BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN with synthetic packets and skb context; FD-only maps/programs, no pins or attachments. Owned run directory removed.

integration.scope: Networking suites plus Raft, membership, snapshots, member restore/bootstrap, main and serve state ownership after integrating main.

legacyRegression: Existing v1 packet and IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP socket bytecode tests passed.

maps.identity: key4/value32; readonly from programs; primary and private alias share endpoint epoch

behavior: Register direct and Service original tuples; reserve return tuple before forward publication.
Prefer source preservation when direct history is complete; use private aliases and bounded candidate ports for hairpin or collisions.
Fence source and backend incarnations; alias source requires enabled owner pair and receiving capability. Capability flags are supplied by the fixture, not actual distributed acknowledgments.
DNAT before egress policy; source rewrite at commit after policy; destination restoration before ingress policy; Service source restoration after policy.
Pending state expires after 5 seconds and cannot authorize replies before commit. Active UDP lifetime 180 seconds; TCP currently conservative 2 hours.
Do not retarget a live binding when backend incarnation or receiver capability changes.
Capacity/interruption tests preserve active owners and foreign reservations; only the original owner can adopt its interrupted claim.
coverage: TCP/UDP source preservation, two Services sharing backend/client port, direct/Service collisions in both orders, self-backend hairpin and multiple alias ports
Per-stage checksum and backend identity order, missing commit, pending expiry, invalid context magic, IPv4 options and zero UDP checksum
Source/backend epoch changes, disabled alias, missing backend identity, receiver capability, sticky backend membership and slot repacking
16-candidate exhaustion plus 7 capacity/contention cases using one-entry kernel maps
implementationNotes: Initial full-parser compiles exceeded the BPF stack limit (516/520/528 bytes). Compact tuple parsing and scratch reuse allowed all four programs to compile and pass the real verifier.
limits: Synthetic BPF packet tests, not live TCP sockets, native/Kata CNI traffic, NetworkPolicy enforcement or physical multi-host proof.
Test harness manually deletes state for capacity recovery; this does not prove background garbage collection.
Full TCP sequence/window/options, FIN/RST handling and safe new-generation tuple reuse are not yet implemented in v2.
Actual policy alias canonicalization, agent attachment, trusted receiver installation acknowledgments, legacy retained-flow migration, upgrade/rollback and bounded GC remain required.
Existing attached v1 map formats/programs are unchanged. IPv6 packet NAT, NodePort and broader Service semantics remain parent requirements.
remaining: Child podster-p9c.10 and parent podster-p9c remain in progress.
